newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
DEVE GOWDA LIKELY TO BE PROJECTED FOR PRESIDENTSHIP

Vice president K.R. Narayanan remains the front runner for the job of Indian President but there appears to be a move to project former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda also for the post. Some sections of the Congress, the Janata Dal and some smaller parties are behind the move. The proponents of Gowda believe in the theory that should there be any obstacle to the elevation of Narayanan, a Dalit or lower-caste Hindu, then Gowda, who belongs to the category of "other backward castes", should be propped up for the President's post.
The Hindustan Times
SENIOR LEADERS PLAN MOVES TO END JANATA DAL CRISIS

Some senior Janata Dal leaders are moving to resolve the crisis thrown up by the organisational elections in the party. Acrimony seemed to be intensifying with central minister Ram Vilas Paswan publicly demanding Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav's resignation. Some senior party leaders are contemplating an intervention to defuse the situation.
The Economic Times
MORGAN STANLEY FINED FOR NORM VIOLATION

The bourse regulator (SEBI) has imposed a penalty of 200,000 rupees on Morgan Stanley Asset Management for violating the provisions of the mutual fund regulations. This is the first time SEBI has penalised any foreign mutual fund for irregularities. SEBI's inspection of the Morgan Stanley mutual fund revealed that it had undertaken asset management activities on behalf of Morgan Stanley Asset Management of New York.
IRA BILL AMENDMENT MAY EXPAND BOARD

The government is likely to amend the draft Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) Bill to enable it to appoint five whole-time members instead of three. This follows a suggestion by the parliamentary standing committee on finance to further broad base it. The change will mean that IRA can now have up to 10 members. The committee has placed its recommendations before the cabinet and final touches are being given to the draft before parliament approves the Bill in the monsoon session.
IDBI TO LEND 2,500 CR RUPEES AS WORKING CAPITAL IN 97/98

The Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) has earmarked 25 billion rupees for disbursal during 1997/98 (April-March) under its working capital loan scheme. These funds will be mobilised from the short term market. The working capital loans will be priced in line with that of the commercial banks. The IDBI's rate of interest for working capital loans will be the minimum term lending rate plus a risk spread. The IDBI will extend working capital loans both in rupee and foreign currency.
RAILWAYS TO RAISE $150 MLN THROUGH EXTERNAL BORROWNINGS

The Indian Railways Finance Corporation plans to raise external commercial borrowings (ECBs) worth $150 million by mid-July. Indications are that the loan will be raised at 0.78 points above LIBOR which reflects overseas investors' confidence in the Railways' financial stability. So far, the corporation has raised ECBs worth $70 million. In the last fiscal year, the Railways were allowed to raise $50 million from the international market. The issue was oversubscribed by $20 million and the Railways was allowed to retain the additional amount.
Financial Express
PREFERENCE SHARES SHOW HOW TO RAISE BANK FUNDS BELOW PLR

An increasing number of Indian corporates are accessing bank finance at rates cheaper than commercial banks' prime lending rates by placing preference shares with profit-making public sector banks. Through this route, they are able to raise money at incredibly low rates of 12 to 13 percent. In effect, the cost of funds for blue chip corporates has dipped about one to two percentage points (100 to 200 basis points) below the public sector banks' prime lending rates, which is now pegged at 14 percent.
COUNTER GUARANTEES MAY LOWER CREDIT RATING

The Finance Ministry said that central counter guarantees to fast-track power projects would lead to a downgrading of the country's credit rating. According to the ministry estimates the annual counter-guarantee liability would work out to around 100 billion rupees. Rating agencies are expected to treat this amount as contingent liability and this will influence the country's overall rating. Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia put forward the arguement while seeking an alternative approach to the counter guarantee cover approved by the cabinet for the 1000mw Bhadravati power project.
Business Standard
LOPSIDED CREDIT FLOW THREATENS MID-CAP FIRMS

Government sources expressed concern at the increasingly lopsided flow of domestic credit towards companies which have foreign equity participation. This has left middle-rung companies purely out of domestic equity. As a result, the middle capital companies are being damaged. Government officials fear that a growth slowdown in this segment could destroy the edifice of industrial development.
ORDER TO ANALYSE DRAFT COMPANY BILL

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has directed the department of company affairs to submit a section by section analysis of the draft companies bill in a month. His decision followed objections to the bill by professional groups, industry organisations and investor protection forums.
TELCO TO LOWER STAKE IN MERCEDES BENZ INDIA

The Tatas controlled TELCO is set to reduce its stake in the joint venture with the German automobile maker Daimler Benz AG and its subsidiary Mercedes Benz from 49 percent to 24 percent. The German multinational has received government nod to raise its equity holding in the joint venture Mercedes Benz India to 76 percent from 51 percent. The Foreign Investment Promotion Board cleared a proposal by Mercedes Benz India for a preferential issue of shares worth 1.79 billion rupees in favour of Daimler Benz. The allotment will raise the equity infusion of the German car maker from 873.4 million to 2.66 billion rupees.
The Observer
TECHNOLOGY UPGRADATION FUND PLAN ACCEPTED

The planning commission has accepted in principle the setting up of a technology upgradation fund for the textile industry during the ninth five year plan. The proposal suggests a corpus of 50 billion rupees for this fund and aims at facilitating upgradation of technologies in the textile industry.
CREDIT OFFTAKE REMAINS SLUGGISH

Despite falling interest rates and a corporate-friendly budget, the credit offtake has failed to show any signs of pick up in the first two months of the current fiscal. This has forced many banks to delay fixing their targets for credit disbursements in 1997/98. Domestic corporates are having second thoughts on all their expansion and diversification plans in view of the large scale entry of foreign companies.
INFLATION DIPS TO SIX PERCENT

The annual rate of inflation for the week ended May 17 dropped to six percent. The rate of inflation, calculated on a point-to-point basis, dipped marginally by 0.4 percentage points to six percent (provisional) as compared to 6.04 percent (provisional) for the previous week. The wholesale price index for all commodities, (base 1981/82 100) moved up by 0.2 percent during the week under review to 323.3 as against 322.8 the week before. The rate of inflation during the corresponding week of 1996 was 4.42 percent.
ICO TO INVEST50 MILLION IN INDIA

The London-based ICO Global Communications will invest $50 million in setting up a satellite access node (SAN) near Delhi. This earth station will be operated by Videsh Sanchar Nigam (VSNL). It is expected to boost VSNL's revenue by $4 million a year. VSNL chairman said the set up will place the company in a strong position to provide communication services via satellite. Further, VSNL's exclusive tie-ups with neighbouring countries like Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh and the Maldives, will mean an additional revenue for providing satellite communication technology and service to these countries. The construction of the SAN has already begun.
